summary: Anthropic details the cybersecurity safety classifiers used in Claude Fable 5's redeployment and publishes an early draft of a proposed cyber jailbreak severity (CJS) scoring framework developed with partners.

mechanisms.reason: The model's availability is stated to have expanded from a restricted deployment back to full global access, implying restored inference volume.
mechanisms.quote: Claude Fable 5 has been re-deployed and is now available globally for all users.

practices.reason: The four-category dual-use classifier taxonomy with detailed examples gives engineering teams a concrete template for scoping their own cyber-misuse classifiers, though it is specific to Anthropic's own classifier design.
practices.quote: we train our safety classifiers to discern between four categories of cybersecurity use, from the most clearly potentially dangerous to the most clearly potentially benign.

practices.reason: The proposed Cyber Jailbreak Severity scale gives a concrete, reproducible scoring rubric across four axes that a security or safety team could apply to grade jailbreaks against their own models.
practices.quote: these factors combine into a banded rating on what we’re calling our Cyber Jailbreak Severity (CJS) scale: None (or “Informational”; CJS-0), Low (CJS-1), Medium (CJS-2), High (CJS-3), and Critical (CJS-4).

notable_reason: Anthropic publishes a detailed, quantitative proposed industry framework for scoring AI jailbreak severity, an unusual level of methodological transparency for cyber-safety practice.
